question: How does keeping girls in school benefit the wider community and economy?

options.A: It guarantees that every family will receive direct cash stipends
options.B: It empowers future workers and boosts family health and financial stability
options.C: It eliminates all local taxes for households with daughters
options.D: It completely stops rural-to-urban migration patterns

explanation: Well reasoned! Educated women earn better incomes, make healthier choices for their children, and help lift their communities economically. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T11#GNS312_U1_T11_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) after a major incident?

options.A: To fulfill government tax requirements for medical centers
options.B: To find out which specific nurse or doctor should be fired
options.C: To calculate total financial damages owed to the patient's family
options.D: To uncover deep underlying system flaws that allowed the error

explanation: Spot on! RCA digs past surface mistakes to find the environmental and procedural triggers that caused the event. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h6)

question: Why is it important to talk about birth control before the patient leaves the clinic?

options.A: To make sure the hospital gets paid by insurance
options.B: To prevent unwanted repeat pregnancies given the rapid return of ovulation
options.C: To push the patient into long-term hormone use
options.D: To make sure the abortion pills keep working

explanation: Since fertility returns so quickly, offering birth control right away protects our patients from unplanned repeat pregnancies. Excellent nursing care! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h8)

question: A nurse who constantly tilts their head downward to read electronic charts is most at risk for what condition?

options.A: Incisional Hernia
options.B: Cervical Spondylosis
options.C: Plantar Fasciitis
options.D: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome

explanation: Correct! Straining your neck downward for long periods puts extra wear and tear on your neck bones over time. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why should nurses advise patients NEVER to put butter or toothpaste on a fresh burn?

options.A: They cause the top layer of skin to fall off immediately
options.B: These substances trap heat inside the tissue and can introduce bacteria
options.C: They react chemically with sweat to produce dangerous acid
options.D: They neutralize cool tap water and make the wound freeze faster

explanation: Spot on! Kitchen remedies like butter act like a blanket, keeping the heat trapped inside and inviting germs that cause infections. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h6)

question: Why do we schedule a follow-up visit a few weeks after starting post-abortion family planning?

options.A: To run routine blood tests for hidden diseases
options.B: To close her medical file and discharge her forever
options.C: To force the patient to buy a more expensive brand
options.D: To check physical healing and see if her birth control method suits her

explanation: Follow-ups let us confirm she is healing nicely and make sure her birth control method is working comfortably for her lifestyle. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h7)

question: A patient with severe internal bleeding from a car crash is most likely to develop which type of shock?

options.A: Neurogenic shock
options.B: Hypovolemic shock
options.C: Anaphylactic shock
options.D: Cardiogenic shock

explanation: Hypovolemic shock is caused by a drastic loss of blood volume circulating in the body. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h5)

question: What does a p-value tell us in a research study?

options.A: The probability that results happened by chance
options.B: The financial cost of running the clinical trial
options.C: The exact dosage of medication given to patients
options.D: The total number of patients included in the sample

explanation: That's right! The p-value tells you the odds that your results are just a fluke or coincidence rather than a real effect of your nursing care. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T3#GNS217_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which of these body areas is a classic, go-to site for giving a subcutaneous injection?

options.A: The sole of the foot
options.B: The abdomen
options.C: The center of the chest
options.D: The palm of the hand

explanation: That's right! The abdomen is a favorite spot for everyday injections like insulin and heparin because it has a nice, accessible layer of fat. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h3)

question: Which breathing sign is a classic warning of severe respiratory distress in a newborn?

options.A: Regular periodic breathing
options.B: Expiratory grunting
options.C: Deep abdominal snoring
options.D: Slow, quiet inspirations

explanation: When a baby makes a grunting sound as they breathe out, it's their way of trying to keep their tiny air sacs (alveoli) open. It's a red flag that they are struggling to breathe. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h6)

question: Which of these is a key thing nurses can do to help with food security?

options.A: Inspecting commercial food processing plants for bacteria
options.B: Operating heavy harvesting machinery on local farms
options.C: Manufacturing nutritional supplements in hospital labs
options.D: Screening patients for hunger and connecting them with resources

explanation: Nurses look out for the whole patient. Asking about food access and linking struggling families to community support programs makes a huge difference. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T024#GNS227_U2_T024_h8)

question: How does empowering clients help with everyday health advocacy?

options.A: It forces patients to follow strict hospital rules
options.B: It encourages patients to voice their preferences and choices
options.C: It removes the need for informed consent documents
options.D: It allows nurses to make medical decisions for the family

explanation: Exactly! When we empower patients, we give them the confidence and tools to speak up and take part in their own health choices. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T7#GNS124_U4_T7_h2)

question: A patient tells you she uses petroleum jelly as a lubricant with her latex condoms. What should be your immediate nursing advice?

options.A: Confirm that petroleum jelly is the ideal choice for extra slip
options.B: Warn her that oil-based lubricants weaken latex and can cause breakage
options.C: Advise her to microwave the jelly first to make it safe for use
options.D: Suggest she switch to oil-based spermicide creams instead

explanation: Brilliant! Oil-based products break down latex rubber super fast, leading to tears. Water-based lube is always the safe choice here! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h6)

question: What makes a Type B drug reaction so tricky compared to other reactions?

options.A: It can always be calculated using the patient's exact weight
options.B: It disappears completely if the patient drinks more water
options.C: It happens suddenly and does not depend on the dose
options.D: It only occurs when the drug expires on the shelf

explanation: Type B reactions are bizarre and unexpected. They can happen out of nowhere, no matter if the dose is tiny or large! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T5#GNS215_U2_T5_h2)

question: A poorly nourished patient is admitted with a severe stomach infection. What physical change makes it easier for germs to get into their blood?

options.A: Increased production of white blood cells
options.B: Damage to the protective lining of the intestines
options.C: Rapid thickening of the stomach lining
options.D: Overproduction of protective stomach acid

explanation: Correct! Lacking enough protein weakens the gut wall, allowing bacteria and toxins to slip past the body's barriers into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T13#GNS313_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why does an RCA team repeatedly ask 'why' an incident occurred?

options.A: To delay reporting the incident to hospital executives for as long as possible
options.B: To prove that the patient contributed to their own injury
options.C: To interrogate nurses until they admit fault for their careless actions
options.D: To trace the chain of events back to the fundamental systemic breakdown

explanation: Asking 'why' multiple times peels back superficial layers of error to expose the real root cause in the workflow or environment. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h4)

question: Which body organ must a nurse monitor closely when a patient is on long-term azole antifungal therapy?

options.A: Bone marrow output
options.B: Visual acuity
options.C: Pulmonary function
options.D: Liver function

explanation: Well done! Azole drugs can stress the liver, so checking liver enzyme blood tests regularly is a key part of safe nursing care. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h6)

question: As an unsterile team member, what is the minimum safe distance you must keep from a sterile field?

options.A: Six feet
options.B: One foot
options.C: Three inches
options.D: Ten inches

explanation: Always stay at least one foot away! This simple rule stops you from accidentally brushing against or contaminating sterile items. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h3)

question: What is the medical term for shortness of breath that happens specifically when a patient lies flat?

options.A: Apnea
options.B: Tachypnea
options.C: Orthopnea
options.D: Dyspnea

explanation: Orthopnea is a classic sign of heart failure where fluid shifts in the lungs when lying down, making breathing difficult. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why is organizing clinical data like a story so helpful?

options.A: It hides negative statistics so the hospital looks better
options.B: It guarantees that hospital administration will approve more funding
options.C: It legally protects the nursing staff from medical malpractice claims
options.D: It guides the audience logically and prevents cognitive overload

explanation: Great job! A clear beginning, middle, and end helps everyone digest heavy facts without feeling overwhelmed. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h3)

question: In a study on medication adherence for high blood pressure, what is the most likely dependent variable?

options.A: Age of the nurse
options.B: Color of the clinic walls
options.C: Blood pressure control
options.D: Distance to the clinic

explanation: The dependent variable is your outcome. Here, we want to see if the blood pressure is successfully controlled at the end of the day! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h7)

question: Why must you put cooked food in the fridge promptly?

options.A: It slows down the rapid multiplication of bacteria at room temperature
options.B: It prevents the food from losing its natural color
options.C: It removes all chemical toxins already produced by germs
options.D: It completely kills all viral spores present in the dish

explanation: Bacteria love warm room temperatures and multiply crazy fast. Putting food in the fridge puts those germs to sleep! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h8)

question: Why are accidental needlestick injuries so scary for healthcare workers?

options.A: They stop the worker from ever touching medical tools again
options.B: They instantly paralyze the hand
options.C: They instantly trigger severe allergies to latex
options.D: They can push infected blood straight into the nurse's bloodstream

explanation: A hollow needle often carries leftover blood from a patient. That's why safe disposal isn't just about the patient—it protects YOU too! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h5)

question: How do deep, slow breathing exercises physically help a patient calm down?

options.A: They increase skeletal muscle tension to release trapped toxins
options.B: They permanently block the adrenal glands from producing cortisol
options.C: They flood the bloodstream with extra adrenaline to burn off energy
options.D: They stimulate the vagus nerve to activate the parasympathetic nervous system

explanation: Deep breathing acts like a brake pedal for your nervous system, stimulating the vagus nerve to switch you from 'fight-or-flight' to 'rest-and-digest.' [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h7)

question: How often should you check and record the mother's pulse rate on the standard partograph?

options.A: Only after delivery
options.B: Once a day
options.C: Every 6 hours
options.D: Every 30 minutes

explanation: Checking the mother's pulse every half-hour helps you catch early signs of exhaustion, dehydration, or distress very quickly. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h5)

question: A patient starts crying while talking about a painful hospital memory during an interview. What should you do first?

options.A: Pause the interview, offer compassionate support, and check if they want to stop
options.B: Turn off the audio recorder and scold the patient for getting upset
options.C: Immediately ignore the tears and rush to finish the next question
options.D: Report the patient to the medical team for psychiatric evaluation

explanation: Compassion over everything! Always put the patient's emotional well-being ahead of your research notes. You're a nurse first. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h6)

question: What should you do first if a bedside monitor shows a sudden drop in oxygen, but the patient looks calm and comfortable?

options.A: Turn off the alarm permanently so it stops annoying staff
options.B: Check the patient and the sensor placement on the finger
options.C: Call the doctor immediately to report a code blue
options.D: Assume the patient is dying and start chest compressions

explanation: Don't panic! Sensors often slip or wiggle loose. Always check your patient and the equipment first before jumping to conclusions. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h2)

question: When would you expect to see bladder irrigation actually ordered for a patient?

options.A: Mild urinary incontinence in an elderly resident
options.B: A routine change of a long-term Foley catheter
options.C: Gross hematuria with active blood clot formation
options.D: Uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection symptoms

explanation: When heavy blood and clots start blocking the catheter, irrigation is the go-to fix to clear the tube and get things moving again. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T23#GNS212_U1_T23_h2)

question: What does the 'use-by' or expiration date on a food package primarily indicate?

options.A: The exact day the food was harvested
options.B: The date the store received the shipment
options.C: The final date the food is safe to consume
options.D: The day the package design was approved

explanation: The use-by date tells consumers when the product is no longer safe to eat due to potential spoilage or bacterial growth. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h5)

question: Which physical sign do patients very often report when they are feeling extremely anxious?

options.A: Rapid heartbeat or palpitations
options.B: Sustained lowering of blood pressure
options.C: Uncontrolled weight gain over days
options.D: Permanent loss of skin pigmentation

explanation: Correct! When anxiety hits, adrenaline surges through the body, frequently causing a racing heart or palpitations. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T1#GNS324_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is an example of indirect gender discrimination in a community?

options.A: Refusing to treat a patient based on their sex
options.B: A sign on a clinic door stating men cannot enter
options.C: Paying female nurses less than male nurses for the same job
options.D: Clinic hours that conflict with domestic caregiving duties

explanation: Indirect discrimination happens when a rule looks fair to everyone on paper, but actually makes it hard for one specific group to get care. You are building strong community nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h3)

question: What is a key role of a nurse acting as a community champion for reproductive health?

options.A: Writing national health insurance budget laws
options.B: Replacing traditional village chiefs in council meetings
options.C: Manufacturing pharmaceutical contraceptive drugs
options.D: Educating and advocating outside hospital walls

explanation: Community champions extend their reach into local spaces to educate populations and advocate for better health practices. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h6)

question: A patient with an enlarged prostate is most likely to experience which problem?

options.A: Complete inability to produce testosterone
options.B: Permanent loss of the sense of thirst
options.C: Severe pain during the production of new sperm
options.D: Difficulty starting and maintaining a urine stream

explanation: Because the prostate surrounds the urethra, swelling or enlargement pinches the tube and obstructs urine flow. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h3)

question: A nurse notices patient call bells take much longer to answer during evening shifts. What is the best systems-thinking response?

options.A: Map out evening workloads, staffing numbers, and task layouts to find the bottleneck
options.B: Tell the evening nurses they are lazy and need to walk faster
options.C: Ignore it because evening shifts are always chaotic
options.D: Punish the nurse sitting closest to the front desk

explanation: Looking for structural bottlenecks instead of throwing blame is the core of systems thinking in nursing leadership. [learn more](GST319_U2_T3#GST319_U2_T3_h7)

question: A pregnant mum taking daily iron pills complains of severe constipation. What is the main reason behind this?

options.A: Iron vitamins cause the stomach to shrink in size
options.B: Iron instantly stops the production of all digestive juices
options.C: Excess iron unabsorbed in the gut binds and hardens the stool
options.D: Iron forces the body to expel water through the skin instead

explanation: Well thought out! The iron that the body doesn't absorb interacts inside the gut, turning the waste firmer and harder to pass. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h3)

question: What happens to red blood cells during a sickle cell crisis?

options.A: Cells swell and burst open prematurely
options.B: Cells become rigid and crescent-shaped
options.C: Cells lose all of their surface proteins
options.D: Cells shrink into tiny spherical shapes

explanation: You've got this! Abnormal hemoglobin S changes the shape of the red blood cells, making them hard and crescent-shaped when they drop off oxygen. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h1)

question: What does the term 'Golden Hour' refer to in trauma care?

options.A: The period required to complete a patient discharge
options.B: The exact hour a shift change occurs in the ward
options.C: The time a patient spends resting after surgery
options.D: The first sixty minutes after a traumatic injury

explanation: The golden hour represents the crucial window where immediate medical and surgical care significantly improves trauma survival rates. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the most common exercise used to strengthen the pelvic floor without surgery?

options.A: Abdominal crunches
options.B: Kegel exercises
options.C: Quadriceps extensions
options.D: Hamstring stretches

explanation: Easy peasy! Kegels are the classic squeeze-and-release exercises that build great pelvic strength. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h8)

question: What is the primary tool midwives use to track the progress of labour on a chart?

options.A: Partograph
options.B: Growth curve
options.C: Bishoff scale
options.D: Apgar chart

explanation: The partograph gives us a neat visual story of how labour is going. It's our best friend for spotting slow progress or fetal distress early! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h3)

question: Why must nurses specifically ask about herbal supplements during a medication history check?

options.A: Hospitals require patients to buy herbal tea during admission
options.B: Herbs can change how prescription drugs work in the body
options.C: Doctors use herbs to replace all standard intravenous fluids
options.D: Herbs are legally classified as Schedule I controlled substances

explanation: Herbal products can speed up or slow down drug metabolism, leading to unexpected treatment failures or toxicity. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why does leadership matter for every nurse, even those without a fancy management title?

options.A: Staff nurses are solely responsible for hospital budgeting
options.B: Formal titles are required before a nurse can influence safety
options.C: All nurses must eventually manage a hospital department
options.D: Bedside nurses routinely guide peers and advocate for safe care

explanation: Leadership isn't just about titles! Even as a student or bedside nurse, you lead whenever you guide a colleague or speak up for your patient. [learn more](GST321_U1_T14#GST321_U1_T14_h1)

question: Why are pills and medications rarely the main treatment for stress incontinence?

options.A: Surgical options and pelvic therapy target the mechanical cause much more effectively
options.B: Medications for stress incontinence always cause permanent kidney damage
options.C: Pills are unable to dissolve inside the human digestive tract
options.D: Doctors prefer lifestyle changes because drugs are illegal for this use

explanation: Since stress incontinence is a physical, mechanical problem of loose support, fixing it requires physical strengthening or surgery rather than drugs. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h7)

question: What does the abbreviation 'gtt' mean in medication administration?

options.A: Gallon
options.B: Dose
options.C: Gram
options.D: Drop

explanation: You nailed it! 'gtt' comes from 'gutta', the Latin word for a drop. You'll spot this when calculating IV drips or giving eye drops. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T8#GNS125_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is the term for emotional exhaustion and numbness that nurses feel after dealing with too much trauma?

options.A: Compassion fatigue
options.B: Post-surgical shock
options.C: Florence Nightingale syndrome
options.D: Professional burnout syndrome

explanation: Compassion fatigue happens when seeing heavy, stressful cases day after day drains your emotional tank. It is totally normal to feel this way, which is why self-care matters! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe injection practice?

options.A: Reusing a disposable syringe after washing it with warm water
options.B: Disposing of used needles immediately into a puncture-proof box
options.C: Using a brand new, sterile syringe for every single patient
options.D: Wiping the rubber top of a medication vial with an alcohol swab

explanation: Never wash and reuse disposable syringes! Washing doesn't kill microscopic germs. Every patient deserves a fresh, sterile syringe. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which room adjustment helps prevent falls on indoor steps for someone with low vision?

options.A: Removing the handrails to give more space for walking
options.B: Polishing the wooden steps until they are shiny and smooth
options.C: Installing dark-colored carpeting that blends with the floor
options.D: Placing bright, contrasting tape on the edge of each step

explanation: Great job! High-contrast markings make it much easier for the patient's eyes to catch where each step begins and ends. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T13#GNS324_U4_T13_h4)

question: What is the main danger if the uterine lining is exposed to constant estrogen without enough progesterone to trigger shedding?

options.A: Rapid thinning and complete wasting of the muscle layer
options.B: Sudden development of ovarian cysts on both sides
options.C: Increased risk of endometrial hyperplasia and cancer
options.D: Permanent closure of the cervix

explanation: Without regular periods to clear it out, the uterine lining can overgrow (hyperplasia) from too much unopposed estrogen, which increases cancer risks over time. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why is planning ahead for disasters so crucial instead of just reacting when patients arrive?

options.A: Reacting on the spot is illegal under standard Nigerian healthcare labor laws
options.B: Casualties never arrive at a hospital unless an advanced warning schedule is posted
options.C: Pre-planning prevents the chaos and confusion that lead to preventable deaths during emergencies
options.D: Waiting for patients to arrive guarantees that medical supplies will never run out

explanation: Think of it like studying for exams early! Planning sets clear roles and routines, stopping a hectic situation from turning into a life-threatening disaster. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h1)

question: How do long-term conditions like diabetes mellitus usually affect our special senses over time?

options.A: They cause sudden and permanent total hearing loss within days.
options.B: They immediately destroy taste buds on the surface of the tongue.
options.C: They prevent the brain from processing any sensory information.
options.D: They slowly damage delicate blood vessels supplying sensory organs.

explanation: Over time, high blood sugar in diabetes slowly damages tiny blood vessels (microvascular damage). This is why chronic conditions often lead to gradual vision changes like retinopathy. You've got this! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T9#GNS311_U3_T9_h1)

question: A head nurse times how long it takes staff to complete morning vitals to eliminate wasted steps. Which management approach is being used?

options.A: Contingency approach
options.B: Systems theory
options.C: Scientific management
options.D: Human relations theory

explanation: Using time studies and analyzing physical movements to optimize workflow is the core of scientific management. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the best way to help an awake, intubated patient communicate with you?

options.A: Using communication boards or writing tablets
options.B: Asking the patient to whisper loudly around the tube
options.C: Relying entirely on family members to translate lip movements
options.D: Temporarily deflating the cuff on the tube so they can talk

explanation: Because the breathing tube sits right through the vocal cords, speaking is impossible. Simple writing pads or picture boards are a nurse's best friend here! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T10#GNS321_U2_T10_h8)

question: What is a primary indication for prescribing central anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Chronic high blood pressure
options.B: Bacterial respiratory infections
options.C: Elevated blood glucose levels
options.D: Parkinson's disease tremors

explanation: Central anticholinergics are frequently used to help control tremors and stiffness in Parkinson's disease. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T7#GNS223_U6_T7_h4)

question: Why do you need to act immediately when a patient gets a chemical splash in the eye?

options.A: Chemicals quickly burn and damage delicate eye tissues
options.B: Waiting prevents the nurse from finding a neutralizing agent
options.C: Delayed washing allows the chemical to crystallize into a solid
options.D: Chemical splashes rapidly lower the normal body temperature

explanation: Time is precious here! Harsh substances start destroying eye cells right away, so washing them out fast stops permanent injury. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h1)

question: Which condition makes cervical traction completely unsafe (a contraindication)?

options.A: Unstable spinal fractures
options.B: Degenerative disc disease
options.C: Cervical radiculopathy
options.D: Mild muscle spasms

explanation: Spot on! Pulling on a broken, unstable spine can cause terrible damage to the spinal cord. Safety first! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T12#GNS221_U1_T12_h3)

question: What does we mean when we say there is a disease outbreak?

options.A: The total eradication of a chronic illness from a population
options.B: A sudden rise in disease cases above normal expectations
options.C: Any single confirmed case of a rare tropical infection
options.D: A predictable seasonal spike in common malaria cases

explanation: An outbreak simply means more people are getting sick than we usually see for that time and place. You've got this! [learn more](GNS313_U1_T10#GNS313_U1_T10_h1)

question: What is Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR)?

options.A: Energy required for vital organ function at complete rest
options.B: Calories burned only during heavy weightlifting
options.C: Total daily calories burned including all movement
options.D: The energy used solely to digest food particles

explanation: BMR is the baseline energy your body needs just to keep your heart pumping and lungs breathing while you rest quietly. No movement required! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T007#GNS227_U4_T007_h4)

question: What is the main job of salivary amylase in your mouth?

options.A: Breaking down complex starches into simpler sugars
options.B: Killing all harmful bacteria entering the throat
options.C: Lubricating the food so it can slide down the throat
options.D: Neutralizing strong acids coming up from the stomach

explanation: Salivary amylase is a helpful little enzyme that gets a head start on digesting carbohydrates right while you chew your food. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h2)

question: What emergency item must always be kept right at the bedside after an amputation surgery?

options.A: A heating pad
options.B: A tourniquet
options.C: An extra pillow
options.D: A bedside commode

explanation: A tourniquet is kept at the bedside just in case there is sudden, heavy bleeding from the surgical site that needs immediate stopping. Safety first! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h3)

question: Which group of vitamins is most likely to build up and cause toxicity if a patient takes too many over a long time?

options.A: Fat-soluble vitamins
options.B: B-complex vitamins
options.C: Water-soluble vitamins
options.D: Amino acid supplements

explanation: Vitamins A, D, E, and K love to hang out in body fat and the liver rather than washing out in urine, which means excess amounts can build up and become toxic. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T005#GNS227_U5_T005_h4)

question: Which IV solution is the ONLY safe one to hang alongside a blood transfusion?

options.A: 0.9% Sodium Chloride
options.B: 0.45% Sodium Chloride
options.C: Lactated Ringer's Solution
options.D: 5% Dextrose in Water

explanation: Normal saline (0.9% NaCl) plays nice with blood! Other fluids like dextrose can cause red blood cells to burst (hemolysis), while Ringer's has calcium that can cause clotting in the tubing. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T11#GNS215_U6_T11_h3)

question: Why is the cricoid cartilage so important in emergency airway procedures?

question: Why are strong people skills even more important in community nursing than in a big hospital?

question: Why is clear paperwork and documentation so important when transferring a patient to a teaching hospital?

question: How does sharing health data across different sectors help the system?

question: Why must a nurse always get explicit consent before referring a survivor to another agency?

question: What is the primary reason lab techs treat every incoming patient sample as a biohazard?

question: A 14-year-old girl wants to stay in school, but her uncle insists she accept an arranged marriage. Which social dynamic is primarily at play here?

question: What are the three main types of names used to identify a medication?

question: Why do disaster nurses need strong resourcefulness and improvisation skills in the field?

question: Which part of the heart acts as its main natural pacemaker?

question: Which organ does the heavy lifting when it comes to adjusting and managing your daily fluid loss?

question: A newborn is experiencing severe breathing trouble and low oxygen levels. What happens to the blood vessels in the baby's lungs as a result?

question: What is the main sign that a patient is truly unconscious?

question: What is the most important thing you can do on the ward to stop germs from spreading?

options.A: Wearing sterile surgical gloves

options.C: Proper hand washing
options.D: Wiping equipment with bleach

question: Why should you avoid twisting your body while carrying a heavy load?

question: Which of these is a classic example of a biological agent?

options.D: Ultraviolet radiation from sunlight

explanation: Biological agents are living organisms like bacteria, viruses, or fungi that can cause infections. Great job keeping your categories straight! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T78#GNS214_U1_T78_h2)

question: What usually happens when a healthcare facility does not have a clear organisational structure?

question: Why is there usually a noticeable difference between 'perfect use' and 'typical use' success rates for barrier methods?

options.A: People sometimes make mistakes or forget to use them consistently

options.C: The materials degrade instantly the moment the package is opened

question: What exactly is metabolism?

question: Why are heart-rhythm medications often stopped before an EPS?

question: Why is it so important for the immune system to tell the difference between 'self' and 'non-self'?

options.A: It allows white blood cells to travel quickly through blood vessels
options.B: It prevents the immune system from attacking healthy body tissues
options.C: It ensures that red blood cells carry enough oxygen to organs
options.D: It helps the body absorb vital nutrients from digested food

explanation: Spotting the difference is key! When the immune system correctly recognizes 'self', it knows not to attack your own healthy cells. Mistakes here are what lead to autoimmune conditions. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h1)

question: How should a nurse collect a urine sample from a patient with a catheter?

question: How should you correctly measure the length of an infant?

question: You are getting ready to give a bed bath. What is the most important thing to check right before you start?

question: An AED has just delivered a shock to a cardiac arrest patient. What should you do next?

question: How long should a patient sit quietly before you measure their blood pressure?

question: In which position should a patient be placed during a gastric lavage to reduce safety risks?

question: How can a lower GNP indirectly lead to poorer health outcomes in a community?

options.D: By directly mutating viral strains in local communities

question: What is the primary role of water inside the human body?

question: Which blood test checks how well the liver is making proteins needed for blood clotting?

question: A client complains that taking a daily pill is too hard with her busy work schedule. What is a great recommendation to discuss?

question: What is the main reason for using a gait belt during a patient transfer?

question: Who is most likely to require custodial care over a long period?

question: A community health nurse wants to help reduce FGM rates in a rural village. Which strategy works best for lasting change?

question: What is the main goal of disease control in public health?

question: Why might giving iron tablets fail to cure a patient's anemia if underlying food taboos are ignored?

question: How is andropause in men different from menopause in women?

question: A teenager finds it hard to say no to friends pushing them into early sex. How can a nurse best help?

question: Why does a family history of early-onset heart disease increase a patient's cardiovascular risk?

question: A patient stays home from work, complains of body aches to their partner, and rests in bed. Which stage of illness behavior is this?

question: A pregnant woman visits the ANC clinic for the first time at 28 weeks. What should the nurse do first?

question: What is one of the most common signs of caregiver burnout in family members looking after an aging relative?

question: Which of these is a key safety outcome indicator in a hospital setting?

question: A patient suddenly feels terrified, has chest pain, and fears they are dying, all within a few minutes. What is happening?

question: Why do adolescent girls need more iron in their diet?

options.B: To prevent the onset of juvenile diabetes

question: Why is the blood-testis barrier (made by Sertoli cells) so important?

question: Which complication is most directly prevented by flushing a gastrostomy tube regularly?

question: How does a community health nurse help families who refuse a recommended hospital referral due to financial worries?

question: Who is famous for unchaining patients at the Bicêtre Hospital in Paris during the moral treatment era?

question: How does low educational background directly affect a client's use of family planning?

question: If a delay in the hospital pharmacy slows down when a ward nurse can teach a patient about their discharge drugs, what does this show?

question: What triggers the kidneys to release erythropoietin (EPO)?

question: Which nutritional deficiency is most common in adolescent girls who have heavy periods and poor diets?

question: Which of the following is considered a microvascular complication of chronic diabetes?

question: Why must you always ask patients about any herbal remedies they take alongside prescription drugs?

question: How do you deflate the retention balloon before taking out a Foley catheter?

question: Your nursing team tries a new handover checklist, but the run chart shows no improvement after two weeks. What should you do next?

options.C: Treat the result as valuable learning to adapt the checklist for another cycle
options.D: Fire the nurse manager and hire an outside corporate consultant

explanation: Don't worry! In nursing quality improvement, a trial that doesn't work right away is just helpful feedback to guide your next try. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h5)

question: How does eating too much sugar over a long time lead to insulin resistance?

options.A: Sugar molecules coat the pancreas and permanently stop it from making any digestive enzymes
options.B: Constant high blood sugar forces the pancreas to oversecrete insulin until body cells stop responding
options.C: High sugar levels destroy every insulin receptor in the liver instantly
options.D: The kidneys block all insulin from entering the bloodstream to protect the heart

explanation: Imagine constantly shouting at someone—eventually, they stop listening! High glucose levels force your pancreas to pump out so much insulin that your body cells eventually tune it out. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h2)

question: Why does a target cell undergo upregulation when hormone levels remain low for a long time?

options.A: To prepare the cell to stop functioning completely
options.B: To turn off the gene expression of the cell
options.C: To increase its sensitivity to the scarce hormone
options.D: To destroy excess hormone molecules in the blood

explanation: Adding more receptors helps the cell catch and respond to whatever small amount of hormone is available. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h5)

question: Which model explains mental illness by looking at biological, psychological, and social factors together?

options.A: Sociocultural isolation theory
options.B: Biopsychosocial model
options.C: Neurological reflex model
options.D: Behavioral conditioning framework

explanation: The biopsychosocial model reminds us that a person is complex. Biology, personal thoughts/feelings, and social surroundings all team up to influence mental health. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T2#GNS314_U1_T2_h3)

question: How do strict professional hierarchies sometimes hurt patient care?

options.A: They discourage junior staff and nurses from sharing critical patient observations
options.B: They ensure that every single medication is administered twice as fast
options.C: They eliminate all forms of communication errors between departments
options.D: They force patients to pay less money for hospital admission fees

explanation: Spot on! When junior staff or nurses feel intimidated by strict ranks, they might hold back life-saving observations out of fear. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h5)

question: A client complains of heavy, painful periods and wants an IUD. Which type should you recommend to help with the heavy bleeding?

options.A: A hormonal IUD that releases levonorgestrel
options.B: A standard copper-bearing T 380A device
options.C: Any IUD, because all types stop bleeding completely
options.D: A plain plastic loop with no hormones or metal

explanation: Hormonal IUDs are great because they lighten the uterine lining over time, which usually means much lighter, less painful periods for the client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h3)

question: When is a new mother at the highest risk for postpartum complications?

options.A: During the third trimester of pregnancy
options.B: Six months after the baby is weaned
options.C: Within the first forty-eight hours after delivery
options.D: At the onset of true labor contractions

explanation: The first 48 hours after birth are critical. This is when heavy bleeding (hemorrhage) is most likely to happen, so close monitoring is a must. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T001#GNS226_U1_T001_h4)

question: Which action directly targets a human reservoir to stop an infection from spreading?

options.A: Boiling all municipal drinking water before distribution
options.B: Placing metal wire mesh over livestock feed storage
options.C: Spraying heavy insecticides around outdoor garbage dumps
options.D: Administering curative drug therapy to clear the pathogen

explanation: Giving medications clears the germs right out of the human body, turning off that human reservoir. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h6)

question: If a large fibroid presses against a patient's bladder, what urinary symptom might she report?

options.A: Severe burning sensation
options.B: Inability to produce urine
options.C: Blood in the urine
options.D: Frequent urination

explanation: When a fibroid grows large, it crowds the bladder and gives it less room to hold urine, leading to frequent trips to the restroom. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T22#GNS216_U5_T22_h4)

question: Why are women biologically more at risk of getting STIs than men?

options.A: The rapid turnover rate of vaginal epithelial cells
options.B: The large area of delicate mucosal tissue in the female reproductive tract
options.C: Lower natural antibody counts in female sweat
options.D: A higher resting internal body temperature in the pelvis

explanation: The fragile lining inside the female reproductive tract easily forms tiny micro-tears during sex, giving germs an easy way to enter the body. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge for monitoring and evaluation in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Inconsistent electricity and poor internet connectivity
options.B: Staff shortages and heavy workloads for nurses
options.C: Fatigue from filling out multiple paper registers
options.D: Unlimited budgets and an excess of electronic tablets

explanation: Resource-limited settings are known for budget constraints and shortages, so having unlimited funds and excess tablets is definitely not the norm! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T21#GNS225_U2_T21_h7)

question: A community health nurse notices high rates of typhoid in a rural village. Which intervention best addresses the underlying determinant of health?

options.A: Writing a research paper on the biology of the typhoid bacterium
options.B: Partnering with local leaders to build protected boreholes for clean water
options.C: Telling every resident to boil their drinking water for five minutes
options.D: Opening a large tertiary hospital in the nearest capital city

explanation: Addressing the root environmental determinant, such as unsafe water infrastructure, provides a long-term solution to waterborne disease outbreaks. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h3)

question: A patient has a stubborn, hard mass of stool that normal enemas can't shift. What procedure is best here?

options.A: A rectal washout
options.B: An intravenous fluid bolus
options.C: A nasogastric tube insertion
options.D: An oral laxative challenge

explanation: When standard enemas aren't strong enough to break up severe blockages, a rectal washout provides the extra mechanical help needed. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h2)

question: What is a major challenge for nursing students facing heavy financial stress?

options.A: Elimination of the need to purchase nursing textbooks
options.B: An immediate increase in clinical ward placement scores
options.C: Free access to high-end medical simulation software
options.D: Balancing exhausting work schedules with studies, leaving little time for rest

explanation: Financial pressure often forces students to hustle outside of school, cutting deeply into study and recovery time. Hang in there—balancing nursing school is no small feat! [learn more](GST321_U8_T9#GST321_U8_T9_h4)

question: Which vaccine is routinely administered to pregnant women during antenatal care visits to prevent a specific neonatal infection?

options.A: Tetanus toxoid
options.B: Measles vaccine
options.C: Oral polio vaccine
options.D: Bacille Calmette-Guérin

explanation: Pregnant women receive tetanus toxoid injections during antenatal visits to protect both mother and newborn against tetanus. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why might you hear a systolic flow murmur in a patient with severe anemia?

options.A: Turbulent blood flow from high cardiac output
options.B: Blood leaking backward through a stiff mitral valve
options.C: Infection of the outer lining of the heart muscle
options.D: A physical hole in the ventricular septum wall

explanation: Because the heart is pumping a larger volume of blood much faster to fight the lack of oxygen, it creates a rushing, turbulent sound that we hear as a flow murmur. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T3#GNS311_U2_T3_h5)

question: A newborn at home is limp, blue, and not breathing well even after being dried. What is your immediate next step?

options.A: Wait patiently for five minutes to see if color returns
options.B: Initiate positive pressure ventilation using a neonatal resuscitation bag
options.C: Administer oral sugar water to the infant
options.D: Wrap the baby tightly and hand it to the grandmother

explanation: When a baby is floppy and not breathing, every second counts. Start bag-valve-mask ventilation right away to help them breathe. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T3#GNS225_U3_T3_h5)

question: What usually happens to uterine fibroids after a woman goes through menopause?

options.A: They calcify and cause acute infections
options.B: They rapidly grow larger and turn malignant
options.C: They multiply and spread to other organs
options.D: They usually shrink due to lower hormone levels

explanation: Because fibroids love estrogen and progesterone, they naturally shrink when hormone production drops after menopause. Nature's way of helping out! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T22#GNS216_U5_T22_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of mixing a patient's blood with anti-A serum in the laboratory?

options.A: To determine the total volume of plasma in the patient's body
options.B: To measure the exact amount of white blood cells in circulation
options.C: To check if A antigens are present on the red blood cells
options.D: To destroy any harmful bacteria hiding inside the blood sample

explanation: Clumping with anti-A serum proves that the patient's red blood cells carry the A antigen. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is the main role of multimodal sensory association areas?

options.A: To store permanent language dictionaries in the brainstem
options.B: To combine inputs from multiple senses into a single experience
options.C: To send initial motor commands directly to skeletal muscles
options.D: To generate raw electrical impulses in the sensory organs

explanation: Multimodal areas act like a mixing desk, taking separate clues from what you see, touch, smell, and hear and blending them into one complete picture of your environment. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h7)

question: Why is continuous reassessment so important in critical care nursing?

options.A: Initial assessments are usually completely incorrect
options.B: Doctors refuse to read reports written only once
options.C: Hospital management requires hourly computer entries
options.D: Patient conditions can change rapidly and unpredictably

explanation: In critical care, a patient who looks calm right now could take a turn for the worse minutes later. That's why we never stop checking! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h9)

question: Why is it important for the nurse to explain the rectal procedure thoroughly before beginning?

options.A: It guarantees that the drug will bypass liver metabolism
options.B: It replaces the need for wearing clean gloves during insertion
options.C: It helps reduce patient anxiety and embarrassment
options.D: It chemically speeds up the breakdown of the suppository base

explanation: The rectal procedure is sensitive and personal; clear communication builds trust and calms the patient. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of partner notification (contact tracing) when dealing with STIs?

options.A: To break the chain of transmission and prevent reinfection
options.B: To punish individuals who engage in high-risk sexual behaviours
options.C: To collect financial penalties for public health clinic operations
options.D: To establish legal liability for disease outbreaks in the community

explanation: It's all about stopping the cycle! Treating partners ensures they don't keep passing the infection back and forth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h6)

question: Which kitchen habit helps prevent accidental grease or boiling water spills?

options.A: Using metal spoons for all cooking tasks
options.B: Turning pot handles inward toward the stove back
options.C: Leaving burners on high heat while cleaning
options.D: Placing hot oil pans near the edge of the counter

explanation: Turning handles inward keeps pots out of reach of children and prevents adults from accidentally bumping into them. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h4)

question: How is quality improvement (QI) different from traditional medical research?

options.A: Quality improvement focuses entirely on blaming staff, while research focuses on patients
options.B: Research uses simple bedside charts, while quality improvement requires complex laboratories
options.C: Quality improvement tracks workflow changes, while research seeks to prove broad theories
options.D: Research has no clinical value, while quality improvement replaces clinical judgment

explanation: Think of it this way: research tries to discover brand-new general knowledge for textbooks, while QI tests quick fixes right there on your local hospital ward! [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h1)

question: When stripping a dirty bed, what is the correct way to handle the used linen?

options.A: Roll it inward toward the center to trap dirt and microbes
options.B: Shake each sheet vigorously to remove loose hair
options.C: Toss the bundle across the room into the laundry chute
options.D: Fold each sheet into a square and place on the floor

explanation: You nailed it! Rolling the dirty linen inward traps skin flakes, dust, and germs so they don't fly into the air or onto your clothes. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of secondary prevention in healthcare?

options.A: Long-term physical rehabilitation
options.B: Early detection and treatment
options.C: Providing end-of-life comfort care
options.D: Stopping disease before it starts

explanation: Secondary prevention catches health issues early through screening so treatment can stop the disease from getting worse. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h1)

question: What does a 'cold' nodule on a radioactive thyroid scan usually mean?

options.A: A hyperactive area that is producing excessive thyroid hormones
options.B: An allergic reaction to the contrast dye used during imaging
options.C: A normal section of tissue unaffected by the radioactive tracer
options.D: An area of low metabolic activity with a higher cancer risk

explanation: A 'cold' spot means the tissue didn't soak up the tracer well. That sluggish activity can sometimes point toward a higher risk of malignancy, requiring a closer look. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why do we have a postnatal referral system in place?

options.A: To reduce the total number of patients visiting government hospitals
options.B: To connect primary clinics with facilities that can handle emergencies
options.C: To collect data for national health research and statistics
options.D: To provide routine immunization schedules for newborns

explanation: Think of a referral system as a bridge! It links small community health posts to advanced hospitals so mothers and babies get rapid help when an emergency hits. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h1)

question: What is an effective strategy to improve nutritional intake in an older adult with poor appetite?

options.A: Waiting until the patient asks for food once a day
options.B: Serving small, nutrient-dense meals more frequently
options.C: Removing all favorite cultural foods from the diet
options.D: Forcing the patient to finish three large meals daily

explanation: Smaller meals are less overwhelming for seniors with low appetite, and making them nutrient-dense ensures they still get enough calories and vitamins. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why are young women biologically more vulnerable to catching sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Faster overall blood circulation to the lower abdomen
options.B: Increased acidity of the normal vaginal flora
options.C: A higher resting body temperature in the pelvic region
options.D: The large area of mucous membrane in the reproductive tract

explanation: Think of the delicate lining inside the female reproductive tract—it has a large surface area that makes it easy for bacteria and viruses to settle in. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why must a hospital conduct manpower planning before hiring new nurses?

options.A: To match the number of available staff with patient care needs
options.B: To decide which brand of uniforms the nursing staff will wear
options.C: To reduce the basic monthly salary of existing nursing staff
options.D: To fulfill government rules without needing actual hospital data

explanation: Manpower planning is just figuring out how many hands we actually need on deck so we don't end up severely understaffed or wasting money. [learn more](GST321_U4_T1#GST321_U4_T1_h2)

question: Over time, why does high blood sugar cause damage to organs?

options.A: Sugar molecules directly injure delicate blood vessels and nerves
options.B: Glucose turns into a toxic acid inside major body organs
options.C: The pancreas stops producing all red blood cells
options.D: Extra sugar blocks the normal flow of oxygen to the lungs

explanation: When blood sugar stays high for too long, it acts almost like sandpaper on the tiny, delicate blood vessels and nerves all over the body. Spotting this early helps us protect our patients! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why are Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Foods (RUTF) so popular for feeding hungry children early in a disaster?

options.A: They have a very short shelf life that forces quick consumption
options.B: They taste sweet and only appeal to adults
options.C: They provide quick nutrition without needing clean cooking water or fuel
options.D: They replace the need for breastfeeding entirely

explanation: When there's no firewood or clean water to cook with, RUTF packets save the day by providing instant, safe nourishment. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T5#GNS315_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why are regular team debriefing sessions important for palliative care nurses?

options.A: They replace the need for taking annual vacation leaves
options.B: They ensure all hospital equipment is cleaned properly
options.C: They are used strictly to punish nurses who make charting errors
options.D: They provide a safe space to share heavy emotional burdens and process grief

explanation: Debriefing allows nurses to talk through difficult patient passings and support one another against emotional burnout. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h7)

question: A patient lacks a specific nutrient in their diet and shows deficiency signs, but labs show their body can easily make similar compounds. What kind of nutrient is this?

options.A: Inorganic mineral
options.B: Essential nutrient
options.C: Inert fiber
options.D: Non-essential nutrient

explanation: If the body can synthesize it independently, it's considered non-essential because we don't strictly have to get it directly from our meals. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h4)

question: A patient in strict isolation cries because no one wants to touch them without gear. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Assure them that the infection is not serious at all
options.B: Remove your gown and gloves to prove you care
options.C: Tell them the rules are necessary and leave the room quickly
options.D: Acknowledge their feelings and spend time talking calmly with them

explanation: Validating emotions and offering supportive conversation helps reduce the psychological toll of isolation while keeping safety intact. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h7)

question: Why shouldn't you give anti-diarrhea medications to someone with a severe bacterial tummy infection?

options.A: Bacterial infections don't respond to meds
options.B: The body needs to flush out the bad bacteria instead of trapping them inside
options.C: They always cause immediate kidney failure
options.D: They make stomach acid dangerously high

explanation: Slowing down the bowels traps toxins and bad bugs right where they can do more damage. Let the body clear them out naturally! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h5)

question: Which piece of information is NOT strictly required on a medication label immediately after dilution?

options.A: The exact dose and concentration prepared
options.B: The patient's favorite hobby or pastime
options.C: The generic or brand name of the drug
options.D: The initials of the nurse who mixed it

explanation: Personal hobbies are irrelevant to medication safety. Labels require identification of the drug, dose, patient, time, and preparer. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h6)

question: Why is creating a confidential and non-judgmental environment crucial when discussing sexual health?

options.A: It guarantees that no chronic illness will ever develop
options.B: It encourages patients to share sensitive concerns and seek help early
options.C: It prevents patients from ever asking questions about medications
options.D: It is required by law to prescribe over-the-counter vitamins

explanation: Patients will only confide intimate struggles if they trust their nurse will treat them with respect and absolute privacy. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT true about integrating different types of healthcare plans?

options.A: Alignment between plans helps prevent wasted resources
options.B: Nurse managers must communicate both upward and downward
options.C: Strategic, tactical, and operational plans must work together
options.D: Operational plans can completely contradict strategic goals without consequence

question: What does the FEFO inventory rule stand for in vaccine management?

options.A: Fastest Entry, Fastest Out
options.B: First Expire, First Out
options.C: Freeze Early, Freeze Often
options.D: Final Evaluation, Final Order

explanation: FEFO ensures that vaccines nearing their expiration date are used before newer supplies to prevent wastage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h8)

question: Which imaging scan is best for spotting hippocampal scarring in psychomotor epilepsy?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.B: Standard skull X-ray
options.C: Bone density scan
options.D: Abdominal ultrasound

explanation: An MRI gives a clear, high-resolution picture of soft brain tissues, making it the top choice for finding tiny scars or shrinking in the hippocampus. Great job! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h4)

question: Why must nurses know that a normal pregnant woman can have a high white blood cell count?

options.A: To determine the correct dose of routine iron supplements
options.B: To avoid misinterpreting a normal pregnancy change as a severe infection
options.C: To calculate the exact date when spontaneous labour will begin
options.D: To prove that the mother's immune system is completely shut down

explanation: Good nursing judgment! Knowing what is normal for pregnancy prevents us from panicking or treating a healthy mum for an infection she doesn't have. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h3)

question: A nurse manager tries out a new handoff checklist with one shift, collects feedback, and compares results to what she predicted. Which PDSA phase is she in?

options.A: Plan
options.B: Study
options.C: Do
options.D: Act

explanation: She is in the 'Study' phase! This is where you look at the data you collected and check how closely it matches your original predictions. [learn more](GST319_U3_T4#GST319_U3_T4_h2)

question: A patient with a blood pressure of 220/130 mmHg complains of a sudden, blinding headache and confusion. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink a large glass of salty broth.
options.B: Wait two hours to see if the headache goes away on its own.
options.C: Tell the patient to lie down and sleep it off until morning.
options.D: Arrange emergency transport to a hospital immediately.

explanation: Severe blood pressure elevation accompanied by neurological symptoms indicates a hypertensive emergency requiring urgent medical intervention. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h6)

question: How is Type II FGM different from Type I?

options.B: It leaves the clitoris completely untouched
options.C: It only involves stitching the vaginal opening shut
options.D: It is performed exclusively using modern surgical lasers

explanation: You nailed it! Type II goes a step further than Type I by also removing the inner labia (labia minora), and sometimes the outer labia too. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h4)

question: Which safety incident is most frequently tracked in rehabilitation hospital quality reports?

options.A: Newborn abductions
options.B: Patient falls
options.C: Surgical site fires
options.D: Radiation overexposure

explanation: You got it! Because rehab patients are actively learning how to move and walk again, preventing and tracking falls is a top priority. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h8)

question: A patient suddenly develops severe shortness of breath and chest pain after a long plane ride. Which condition should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Pulmonary embolism
options.B: Chronic bronchitis
options.C: Essential hypertension
options.D: Left ventricular failure

explanation: Immobility during a long trip can lead to blood clots in the legs that break off and travel to the lungs, causing a pulmonary embolism. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h7)

question: When breast cancer cells start to spread, where is the very first place they usually travel?

options.A: The main coronary artery system
options.B: The axillary lymph node network
options.C: The superficial jugular veins
options.D: The central spinal fluid pathway

explanation: The lymph fluid from the breast drains straight toward the armpit, making the axillary nodes the first station cancer cells visit on their spread. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h2)

question: A patient with an advanced illness is physically stable, but their family looks completely exhausted and anxious. What should you do as the nurse?

options.A: Ask the doctor to discharge the patient immediately to relieve stress
options.B: Tell the family to go home and rest until the patient's condition worsens
options.C: Focus only on the patient since their physical vitals are stable
options.D: Include the family's coping capacity as part of your ongoing assessment

explanation: When the family is worn out, it affects the patient too! Checking in on how the family is coping is a vital part of good nursing care. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T4#GNS321_U4_T4_h2)

question: In data with a positive skew, how do the mean and median usually relate to each other?

options.A: The mean and median remain identical regardless of the direction of the skew
options.B: Both the mean and median drop to zero because skewed data cannot be measured
options.C: The median is always higher than the mean because it ignores all low values
options.D: The mean is typically higher than the median because extreme high values pull it upward

explanation: A positive skew has a long tail of high numbers, which drags the arithmetic mean higher than the middle median value. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T4#GNS217_U4_T4_h5)

question: A nurse wants to teach a rural community how to prevent cholera. What is the best way to communicate?

options.A: Distribute dense medical textbooks written in advanced technical English.
options.B: Post warning notices exclusively on international websites.
options.C: Use local languages and collaborate with respected community leaders.
options.D: Rely entirely on unspoken signs posted without any translation.

explanation: People listen best to trusted community voices speaking in their own language. Communication is key in public health! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h6)

question: What is the main goal of using mobile outreach teams in immunization programs?

options.A: To sell prescription medications directly to rural households
options.B: To reach children living in remote or hard-to-access communities
options.C: To collect taxes from local markets on behalf of the government
options.D: To replace permanent primary health centers in major cities

explanation: You got it! Mobile teams bridge the gap so children in hard-to-reach areas don't miss out on life-saving vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T69#GNS214_U1_T69_h8)

question: Which of these is a typical part of harsh traditional widowhood practices?

options.A: Forced isolation and denial of basic hygiene and nutrition
options.B: Mandatory medical checkups at a local government clinic
options.C: Immediate financial compensation provided by the extended family
options.D: Celebration of the woman's new status as head of the household

explanation: Sad to say, many widows face difficult isolation, poor sanitation, and restricted food as part of old mourning customs. As nurses, we are here to support them heal! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T1#GNS312_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is a major limitation of relying only on BMI to judge someone's health?

options.A: It changes drastically depending on what the patient ate for breakfast
options.B: It requires expensive laboratory equipment to calculate properly
options.C: It only works accurately for newborn infants and toddlers
options.D: It cannot distinguish between weight coming from muscle mass versus body fat

explanation: Muscle weighs more than fat, meaning a very muscular athlete might show up as overweight on a BMI chart even when they are super healthy! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T3#GNS112_U6_T3_h6)

question: Why is it usually unhelpful to just punish a nurse after a mistake happens on the ward?

options.A: It stops other staff members from documenting patient care properly
options.B: It ignores the underlying system flaws that allowed the error to happen
options.C: It makes the nurse work faster during the next emergency shift
options.D: It increases the budget available for buying new medical equipment

explanation: Exactly! Blaming just one person doesn't fix a broken system. To keep patients safe, we have to fix the root causes so the same mistake doesn't happen again. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T7#GNS312_U5_T7_h3)

question: Which blood marker is commonly measured to help screen for prostate disorders?

options.A: Plasma glucose
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Serum creatinine
options.D: Prostate-specific antigen

explanation: Elevated levels of prostate-specific antigen can indicate inflammation, enlargement, or cancer within the prostate. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which hormone is released by the adrenal glands to help raise heart rate and blood pressure during shock?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Insulin
